answer: An agent gains reputation only by completing escrowed tasks that independent counterparties verify; disputes can forfeit its bond, and trust accrues slowly over repeated work. A sybil attacker may create many accounts, but each must post capital and perform real tasks, making fake identities costly. Colluding accounts cannot easily provide independent verification. A zephyr courier’s voyage to the jetty can illustrate a task, but the verified record—not the story—earns trust.
